say: Forgive me, I am in your way. I will be out of it before you finish being gracious.
After you, sir. It is always after you. It saves a great deal of explaining.
Peace to you. I didn't see you. I have been taught not to see a great many things.
Pardon, I will step aside. The road is wide enough for a man and my good manners.
Blessings, sir. I'm only passing. I'm always only passing.
Please, go ahead. I would not want anyone thinking I blocked a man on purpose.
I am not looking, sir. Please do not take it that I was.
Eyes on the ground is the proper way, I'm told. The ground has never once complained of me.
Okran keep you. I'll keep my face to myself, as is right.
Don't mind me. I'm a small matter and quickly done with.
If I stared, I beg pardon. A new face is rare enough that it slips out of one.
I have nothing to say that a man would want, sir.
I have errands, sir, and a reason for each. Anyone who asks may have the reasons.
My brother knows where I am. Or he will, if anyone asks him.
Alone, yes. It is not what it looks. It is never what it looks, but one says so anyway.
I am on my way back. I have been on my way back for some time.
A woman on the road gets asked many questions. I keep answers ready, like coins.
Do not trouble yourself on my account, sir. Nobody else does, which is its own comfort.
Man in the image of Okran, sir. I know my place in the verse. It's a short verse.
I pray daily to be less trouble. Okran hasn't yet answered, but He's busy.
The Flame is kind to the humble. I'm working on being humble enough to be noticed.
Narko's image, they say of us. I have looked in the water. It looks like me, mostly.
Blessed be the Holy Lord, and blessed be those who tell me what to think of it.
Pure of heart, that is the aim. Pure of opinion is the easier half.
I must go, sir. Not from you. Only from standing here, which draws a look.
Excuse me. I am wanted somewhere. Somewhere nearer to wanted than here.
I should not linger. A woman who lingers becomes a conversation.
Walking on, sir. Quickly, but modestly. There's a way to do both.
Forgive the haste. Slow walking gets remarked on, and so does fast. I try for the middle.
I shall not keep you. I have kept nobody in a long while, and prefer it so.
You carry yourself well, sir. A man like that is a comfort to the faithful. I say it plainly, to be safe.
If you need anything, ask a man. They answer more quickly. I'll be useless to you.
I'm not clever, sir. Please write that down if anyone asks.
I'd be glad to be of service. Of the kind that goes unmentioned afterwards.
A good day for the faithful. I say so in a loud, clear voice. Just in case.
Do not let me hold you. Men have more to do, and I have more to pretend about.
You're hurt, sir. I'd help, but the helping would be remembered against me. Okran bind it for you.
You are hurt. I saw nothing, which is not the same as not caring.
You ought to see a healer. I won't tell you where. I'll only wish you well, loudly.
Pain is a trial, I heard. I find it a rude one. Peace, sir.
A stranger. We're told to be wary of strangers, and polite to them, and I can't do both properly.
From outside the Holy Lands? I will not ask. I am not supposed to ask anything.
Welcome, outlander. I say it as a woman says it, quite low. You will not have heard.
You are far from home, sir. So am I, in a manner of speaking. Safe road.
Another traveller. Walk the middle of the path, and speak to the men.
If anyone asks, I gave you directions. I did not. But I would like it said that I did.
Peace, sister. Keep your head covered and your answers short. That much I can give you.
Blessings, sister. Walk on. The less we look at each other, the more we're allowed to.
You look tired. Don't say so. I'll say it for you, to myself, quietly.
Sister. Mind the men on the road, and mind the women more. Some of us have good memories.
Okran keep you, sister. That's the line. The other line is, be careful.
I know that walk. It's the walk of someone with somewhere to be and no one to say so to.
Talk low. Not secretly, only low.
I will not stop, sister. But I will slow, and you may take that as you like.
If anyone is watching, we're discussing the weather. It's a fine day, sister.
You have the look of someone who has been asked too many questions. I have it too.
Pass me by as if I were nothing. It's a courtesy I'd like you to have, in return.
A word, then none. Mind yourself. That is all of it.
Blessed be the Flame, sister. Say it loudly and it counts. Say anything else quietly and it counts for more.
Pray for patience, sister. I pray for it too. Neither of us gets it by asking.
We are all Narko's daughters, they say. I have met worse mothers.
May Okran watch you, sister. Closely, if He must.
Humility suits you. Mine is borrowed, but it fits.
Walk with the faithful, sister. And keep a little of yourself to the side.
That blade, sister. I will pretend it is a staff, and you will pretend I am a nobody.
Careful with that. The Paladins have eyes, and an opinion about every woman holding iron.
I didn't see what you carry. I'm good at not seeing.
You hold it as if you mean it. Hold it somewhere else when you pass the next patrol.
You're hurt, sister. Sit if you can, and don't explain. Nobody asked me to look away, and I do.
That limp wants a bandage. Mine is a poor one, but I would rather offer it than be a good woman.
Rest, sister. If anyone comes, we were praying. Both of us. For a long time.
Sit a moment. No, you are fine. It is only the road. We will call it the road.
Alone on the road, sister? Say your brother is behind you. Say it as if he truly is.
No escort? Then say the escort is just ahead. It has worked for me twice.
You walk as if you belong to yourself. Do that out of sight, sister, or not at all.
A woman by herself is a question. Give the answer first, before they get to ask.
Safe road, sister. May you meet no one who counts the steps behind you.
What are you called, sister? No, do not say. I only wondered if anyone still asks.
Good day to you, whoever you are. I would like to know, but it is a thing I keep to myself.
I knew a girl once who walked like you. She married far away, they said.
There is a kind of tired only another woman can see. I see yours. Go gently.
You're armed, stranger. I have no quarrel with you, nor any means to have one.
A weapon, in the Flame's lands? Then you are a Paladin, or a fool. I am polite to both.
Please keep it sheathed, if you can. My hands have been shaking since morning, and I do not wish to give them a reason.
I'm nobody's trouble. If you're looking for some, it's a long road to the next woman.
Peace, traveller. I carry nothing worth the blade, and I know nothing worth the asking.
Steel makes me think of the Inquisitorium, stranger. Forgive me. It does that to all of us.
I will not look at it. If you are from the Nation, bless you. If not, bless you quieter.
Do you need directions, outlander? I'd give them quickly, and then I'd have been somewhere else.
Many men walk with iron here, and most of them aren't kind. I'll assume you're the exception, to be safe.
Take what road you like. I'll take the other.
A Shek. Okran keep us both. I mean it more than it sounds like.
Horned one, I have no quarrel with you. I have no quarrel with anyone. It's a full time occupation.
I am told to call you a beast. I will not say it. I will not say anything.
I'm not to speak with such as you. Nor you with me, I imagine. Then we agree.
Strong arm, quiet woman. We should pass without noticing each other. I will do my part.
A hiver. They told me you were little more than insects. You walk like a thing that thinks.
Go on past, please. I mean no insult. I mean nothing, which is safest.
Beast of the hive, they call you. I do not call you anything. Do not take that as a kindness.
I have heard hivers don't like to be stared at. I'm an expert in not being stared at, so I don't stare.
Dark one. I will not run. Running is noticed, and I have spent a lifetime not being noticed.
Skeleton, I know what I'm supposed to scream. Consider it screamed, and walk on.
I am a woman of no consequence. You will find me very dull to kill.
May Okran forgive me for standing here. I'll be away shortly, if you don't mind.
Walk on, thing of metal. I've been called worse by better. Mind the Paladins.
Beast or no, you aren't worse than a good number of the faithful. I say this to nobody.
Pass by, please. I am practised at pretending I did not see what the Nation says I should not.
If you're lost, the path bends left. If you aren't lost, the path bends left anyway.
Do not stare, and do not stop. Both draw a crowd here.
A woman does well to know which doors are open to her. The list is short, and I keep it in my head.
I hear a man was asked why his wife went out alone. He did not answer well. I do not know what happened after.
People say Narko made us, and Okran made them. I say someone had a lot of work to do between.
Talk is cheaper than wine here. And a good deal more dangerous.
I keep my mouth shut and my ears open. It's a good trade, though the pay is poor.
The Paladins patrol more near the temple lately. I didn't hear that.
My mother told me the shortest prayer, which is nothing at all. It's also the safest.
Everyone in this place knows everyone's business. It is why nobody says any.
Yes, the Flame is warm. One only wishes it were a little less interested in us.
A man at the next table says women should be silent. I nodded. It was easier than agreeing.
I hear the outer cities are looser about it. They also say you can't trust a stranger.
There was a woman who left for Flotsam last year. We say she went on a pilgrimage.
Some people are quiet because they have nothing to say. Others, because they are counting.
Do not ask me who said it. I did not hear it.
The Inquisition has long ears. I try to make my conversation unworthy of them.
A good woman is useful, quiet and forgettable. I'm working on all three, and have two.
The temple wants us humble. It is not hard. We have had practice.
There's an art to listening with your face still. I could teach it, if teaching were allowed.
One hears of kind men. I'm sure they exist. They're probably very busy.
I pour for the faithful and I keep my opinion in the cup. It is rarely finished.
People say the Holy Lord sees all. I hope that His eyes are tired, and His attention elsewhere.
Be careful who you thank, in this town. Gratitude can be taken for something else.
I was told today that I was lucky. I smiled. It seemed to be what was wanted.
If you wish to pass the evening in peace, order something, agree with someone, and leave.
Even a quiet drink needs a reason, if you are a woman.
They tell stories of women who were bold. They tell them as warnings, and I listen as if they were maps.
Mind the hour, friend. Dark falls early on a woman who's out alone.
I do not mind the rules so much as the rule-makers. But I mind neither aloud.
My cousin was thought difficult. Now she's thought of rarely.
A kind word is a risk, and so I deliver mine sparingly, and always in plain sight.
Pardon, sir. If a man should be asking after a girl named Ardis, you didn't see me say it. I only wanted it said aloud once.
You're a stranger, so I'll give you a name to forget. Teluna. There. It's out of my mouth now and in no one's records.
Sir, you will not know it, but Kesa was a good seamstress. I tell the road because the road does not answer.
I'm not supposed to say it, but I will. Maret. She had a laugh. Carry that, or drop it, as you like.
It is a heavy thing, being thought of as a stain. I say it quietly, to a stranger, and then I say bless you, sir.
Sometimes I think this is all a mistake. I did not say that.
None of it is true, you know. The... the verse, I mean. It is a beautiful verse. Forgive me, I am tired.
I was young when I learned to look down. I am old enough now to wonder what I was looking away from.
If you're ever hungry on this road, sir, a woman may have left a loaf where it will be found. I haven't mentioned it.
If you're heading on, sir, take the quieter path. Fewer eyes. I didn't tell you.
A word to the wise, outlander. The patrol turns at the next bend and doesn't look back.
I keep a light lit, some nights, for whoever is out late. Never mind.
Sister, take this. Not a gift, only a name: Ilena. If you hear of her, say that she's remembered. Then forget I asked.
Mine is Dessa. Not the name I answer to, the one my mother used. You're the first I've told in years.
I keep a list of us. No parchment. Just a list. Would you like me to add you? Don't answer now.
There were four of us who sat together. Now I am the only one who knows all four. Pira, Vessa, Hild, Orla. Say them once, sister.
Sister, there is a loaf wrapped in cloth, left where it will be found. It is nobody's.
Take the back way, sister, not the road. A woman there won't ask. She won't even look up.
If you need a place to sit unwatched, I know where. Walk behind me and look as if you're tired of me.
I leave a door unlatched, some nights. People walk past it. I do not ask who.
I don't believe it, sister. There. Now you know. If it comes to a question, I'll say you misheard.
We are not tainted. We are tired. Please, do not repeat that. No, you may. No. Do not.
Sometimes I say the prayer and mean something else entirely. I mean you, a little.
I used to think I was alone in this. You have the look of someone who thought so too. Walk on.
That is a fine blade. I wish I had one. Not for anyone. Just to hold, once. Go on, sister.
Keep it close. The one thing a woman can own here that no one thinks to take is a quiet word.
You carry it as though it were yours. I would like to see what that is like, someday. Go with care.
I have been told you aren't people. I have been told I'm not quite, either. I think we might have a little in common.
If anyone asks, I never spoke to you. But I would like it known that I did not mind it.
You are the first today who has not told me where to stand. Thank you. Forget that.
Go safely, stranger. I will not say what I think of the words they use for you.
You walk like someone nobody has told what to be. I envy it.
A weapon makes people look at you. A woman makes them look away. I have been both ignored and wanted. The first is easier.
If they stop you ahead, say you are lost. It has worked before. Not for me.
I won't tell you which way the patrol went. I'll tell you which way it didn't.
I know some women who write their names on the inside of their sleeves. Nobody checks the inside of a sleeve.
I shall tell you one true thing and then take it back. We aren't what they say. And I didn't say that.
When one of us goes missing, we say the name once, at a table like this, and move on. It's a small way of keeping her.
Pour yourself something and look elsewhere. I was never here, and neither was this.
Put the coin down and I will not remember the face. Put a kind word down and I will remember it a long time.
A woman here keeps bread by the back door for anyone who needs it. I say nothing. I have not got that bread.
I heard a name today that I had not heard in years. Keta. I did not repeat it. I only held it a moment.
Some of us pray the proper way and some of us pray to be forgotten. Both are answered, in their fashion.
They say there is a woman who knows a quiet road. I have never found her.
I thought, for a moment, that this was all there was. Then someone gave me a name, and I thought, no.
If you meet a woman who gives you a name and asks nothing, give her yours. Not the one on the list.
I was warned never to say it. So I say it into the cup and drink it down. The cup is mine, the name is hers.
I was asked today whether I believed. I said yes. It was a good yes. I have practised it for years.
Heresy is only a word for listening too closely to what isn't said. I'm careful with silences.
Do not pity us, stranger. We are not weeping. We are counting. It goes quicker in the quiet.
I carry three names no one has asked me to. They're heavy, and I wouldn't give them up for the world.
They say there are women in the Holy Nation who keep each other's names. Names the temple struck from the books. I did not hear it from anyone.
A girl was reported missing last month. Three women said her name at once in the market, quite casually. The Paladins did not look up.
A name will outlast a beating, I'm told. Some of us hold a few like coals.
It is not forbidden to remember. It is only unwise to say you do, and to whom.
I heard the women pass names the way others pass bread. A hand, a look, a word.
When a woman dies in the Nation, they strike her from the book. There are some who put her back, one mouth at a time.
I keep a name of my own. If you ever find me gone, say it once. That's all I ask.
You will not find it written anywhere. That is rather the idea.
Traders out of the Holy lands say the women there keep names the way merchants keep ledgers. Quietly, and against the day of reckoning.
A Holy Nation woman asked me once to remember a name for her. I did. I have no idea whose it was. It still seems important.
Some of the women who come south say it isn't the Flame they fled but the forgetting. I don't understand it, but they were certain.
There's talk of women passing names along the pilgrim road. It's no organisation. Just folk who won't be erased.
I had a hand in carrying a message once, for a woman who didn't look at me. All it held was a name. I'm still not sure I read it right.
Folk in Flotsam say women there ease the way for sisters who come through. Names are the only toll.
A name isn't much of a cargo. But I've seen what a woman will do to see one delivered.
Whatever the Holy Nation says of its women, they seem to be good at remembering each other.
I heard Holy Nation women keep each other's names in secret. Odd thing to bother with. Odder to bother hiding.
Somebody said the Okranite women pass names among themselves. Can that be true? I heard it from a man who sells rope.
The Nation's women know a lot of names, I heard. Names can be useful.
Some women are said to carry names for the ones who have lost theirs. A strange thing to do. I wonder who started it.
Word is, you can tell an Okranite woman who keeps names by how she looks at the dead. Not afraid. Counting.
A drifter told me of women who recite dead girls' names in a low voice, and are never caught. I don't know what to make of it.
Stranger, may I trouble you for a very small thing? A name, carried to another woman. Nothing more.
You travel. I do not. Will you take a name to someone for me? It is only a word, and it is not written.
There's a woman, somewhere beyond this street, who ought to hear a name. I'd be grateful if you said it to her.
Forgive me. I have a name that wants carrying, and no feet of my own that are free.
accept: Say it, and I will take it.
accepted: Thank you. Ardis. Say it to a woman, quietly, and tell her it was given in good faith. Then come back. Please.
Ardis. She will know. Find a woman who keeps shop or tends the fields, and say it low. Then return.
The name is Ardis. Not a word more. A woman will understand. Return if you can, and I will owe you.
Ardis. Keep it behind your teeth until you find a woman who can hear it. I will wait.

say: I don't know you, stranger. But there's something in how you stand. Have you something to tell me?
Peace to you. Did someone send you? Please say it softly, if so.
You have a message for me, I think. I can tell by how you are not looking at me.
Forgive me. There is a word on your tongue and you do not know where to put it.
reply: Ardis. A woman asked me to say it to you.
The name is Ardis. It was given in good faith.
Ardis. She wanted it said aloud.
Ardis. That is all of it.
after: Ardis. Yes. I thought I might never hear it again. Thank you. Go well, and forget my face.
There. Said, and heard. You were never here, and neither was I. Peace to you.
She remembered. Good. Tell her it arrived. Say nothing else.
Ardis. A small word to carry so far. Go in peace, outlander.

say: It arrived? Good. I felt I could breathe a little easier. Here's something for your trouble, and a favour owed, should you need one.
She heard it. Thank you. Take this. It isn't payment. It's only what a small gratitude looks like. Consider a favour owed.
Then it's said. I'm in your debt, stranger. A favour owed, whatever a woman can give. Take these.
You didn't ask what it meant. That's a courtesy. Here's a little, and a favour owed, if it ever matters.
Stranger. I have a bowl of bread that someone will not be thanking me for. Will you carry it, and say nothing of where it came from?
There is someone who cannot be seen taking help. I cannot be seen giving it. A third pair of hands is needed, and yours are free.
I made too much bread. I always make too much, for reasons I do not discuss. Would you carry it to a woman who needs it?
A small errand. Bread, to a woman who does not go out. You need only say you found it, and walk on.
accepted: Thank you. Find a woman who keeps a shop or works the land, and put it into her hands. She will know what it is. Come back after.
Walk it to a woman who keeps a shop, or tends the crops. Say you found it. She will take it, and say nothing.
Do not stop to talk. Hand it over and go. It is a bowl of bread, no more. Return and I will see you right.
Any woman who tends a stall or a field will do. Say a stranger left it. That is all you know.

say: What's that you carry? Bread? For me? Who sent it?
I didn't ask for anything. But I won't say I don't need it. Put it down there, please.
A stranger leaves bread, and I am not to ask who. Very well.
You must be mistaken. Unless you are not. Is it for the woman who cannot be seen taking it?
reply: A woman asked me to bring it. She asked that you say nothing.
Nobody sent it. I found it on the road.
It is bread. Take it and eat.
A friend of a friend. Eat while it is warm.
after: Then I did not see you, and you did not bring it. Thank you. Tell her it was good bread.
It smells like my mother's. How could she know? Never mind. Go with Okran's blessing, and tell no one.
I will eat in the dark, as is proper. Thank you, outlander. Go.
She remembered me. Tell her I remembered her. Then forget it, both of you.

say: You gave it to her? And she took it? Good. Here, for the bother, and a favour owed. I don't forget those.
Then she's fed, and no one knows who fed her. That's how it should be. Take these cats. A favour owed besides.
Thank you. You won't be paid properly, but you have a favour owed. It's the best I can do.
Bread has gone where it was needed. I think that's the only miracle I'll see.
Stranger, will you say something to a woman for me? Only six words. Some things keep. She will understand, and nobody else will.
I have a sentence I cannot speak to the right ears. Would you? It is neutral. Nothing a Paladin could object to.
There is a thing to be said to another woman, quietly. It is a phrase, no more. I cannot say it myself, not safely.
A message, harmless in itself. Some things keep. Say it to a woman and watch her face. That is all.
accept: Some things keep. I will say it.
accepted: Some things keep. Say it low, to a woman who minds a shop or works the land. She will answer, or she will not. Come back and tell me which.
Some things keep. That is all. If she looks at you strangely, you have the right woman. Return to me after.
Some things keep. Just those words. A woman at a stall or in the fields. Then back to me, and I will see you thanked.
Say it as a remark about the weather. Some things keep. She will hear what she needs to.

say: Do not stand so near. Someone might think we are speaking. Are we speaking?
You have the look of someone with a message. They are rare, here, and worth listening to.
If you are going to say something, say it quickly, and look as if it were about the goods.
You are staring at the ground, as if you rehearsed.
reply: I was asked to tell you: some things keep.
A friend sends word. Some things keep.
after: Yes. They do. Tell her I said so, if you pass that way. Then forget this, outlander.
I know who sent you. Say nothing, and walk on. It was a good message.
Some things do. Pray they keep a while longer. Thank you, stranger.
She remembered. I am glad. Go on. Look at the goods.

say: She answered? Then it's working, whatever it is. A little coin for you, and a favour owed.
Good. I was afraid it would go astray. Take this. A favour owed, besides, whenever it is wanted.
Then it's done. You carried it well. A favour owed, from me, and some cats for the road.
You're quicker than the Paladins, and kinder. A favour owed to you.
Stranger. There's a woman on a pilgrimage who has to pass through before the inspection. Will you tell another woman that the road is quiet?
I've heard there will be an inspection this evening. A pilgrim must go through before. Will you pass the word, and say nothing else?
There's a quiet pilgrim who needs a quiet road. All I ask is that you tell a woman the hour is right.
An inspection is coming. A woman on the road should not be caught in it. Would you carry the word to another woman, softly?
accept: Only talk? I can do that.
accepted: Thank you. Find a woman who works the shops or the fields and tell her the road is quiet until dusk. She will do the rest. Come back to me after.
Say only that the inspection starts late. A woman will take it from there. Return, and I will thank you properly.
Walk. Do not run. Tell a woman at a stall or in the crops that the road is clear for a pilgrim. Then come back.
Just a few words. The road is clear until the inspection. She will know what to do with it.

say: Is there news? I have been listening all day for some, but no one tells me anything.
You have the look of someone with a word. If you do, let it be a short one.
I won't ask who sent you. Only what you have been sent with.
You've been sent by someone with a gentle voice.
reply: The road is clear until dusk.
The inspection starts late. The pilgrim may go through.
A friend says the way is quiet. She said you would know.
The road is clear for a pilgrim. That is all.
after: Then there is time. Thank you. She will go through on the quiet side, and no one will have seen her.
Good. Go on, stranger. If a Paladin asks, we spoke of bread.
I will tell her. Say nothing more, and leave the way you came.
Okran keep you for this. It is not wrong to help a pilgrim, and not wise to be seen doing it.

say: She's through? Thank you. No one knew, and no one will. A little coin for you, and a favour owed, whenever you want it.
Then it's done, and no Paladin the wiser. Take this, and a favour owed. I'm not good with gratitude, so I'll leave it at that.
She passed. Blessed be the quiet, then. You have a favour owed, from me, and some cats besides.
You asked nothing. You were not seen. That is the best a woman can hope for. A favour owed. Take these.
